lead.headline: Fed raises rates a quarter point, first hike since 2023
lead.dek: Unanimous 12-0 vote lifts the target range to 3.75%-4%; Warsh says inflation 'too high and has been for too long'
body: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point Wednesday, to a range of 3.75% to 4%, its first increase since 2023 and a break with President Donald Trump's repeated demands for cuts. The Federal Open Market Committee approved the move on a 12-0 vote, the Fed said in its statement.

"Inflation remains elevated," the committee said, adding that the action "will support a timelier return" to its 2% goal. Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters that "the plain fact is that inflation is too high and has been for too long." Annual inflation ran 3.4% in August, NPR reported, with gasoline more than a third of the monthly rise as the Iran war lifts fuel prices.

Projections released with the decision show policymakers expect on average one more quarter-point increase this year and none in 2027, NPR reported. Trump posted that rates "should be 1% or less," then told reporters he still has confidence in Warsh, who took over in May, Al Jazeera reported. The Dow fell 630 points on the day, NBC News said.

briefs.headline: Johnson recesses House early, sidelining Hegseth impeachment
briefs.summary: Speaker Mike Johnson sent the House home Wednesday to campaign, heading off Rep. Thomas Massie's push to force a vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Johnson called it "a stunt."

briefs.headline: House sends Russia sanctions bill to Trump's desk, 262-159
briefs.summary: The package, which cleared the Senate 86-11 in August, targets Russian officials, companies and banks and lets the president impose tariffs on top buyers of Russian oil and gas, NPR reported.

briefs.headline: Judge gives 20 years to man tied to Kabul airport bombing
briefs.summary: Mohammad Sharifullah, 28, was sentenced Wednesday in Alexandria, Virginia, for supporting ISIS-K; prosecutors said he scouted a route for the 2021 attack that killed 13 U.S. service members.

briefs.headline: Flash flooding kills 3 on the Navajo Nation in New Mexico
briefs.summary: Two adults and a child were swept away near Newcomb early Wednesday, tribal police said, as the National Weather Service warned of excessive rain across the Four Corners through Thursday.

briefs.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 10 across Ukraine in a day
briefs.summary: Regional officials reported deaths in five oblasts from Dnipropetrovsk to Odesa; Ukraine's Air Force said it downed 124 of 157 drones and seven of 10 cruise missiles.

briefs.headline: Kosovo tribunal sentences ex-president Thaci to 25 years
briefs.summary: The EU-backed court in The Hague convicted Hashim Thaci on Wednesday of murder, torture and arbitrary detention in the 1998-99 war; three co-defendants got 13 to 25 years.

briefs.headline: War-damaged Gaza City building collapses, killing 21
briefs.summary: Palestinian Civil Defence said at least 21 people died when the al-Saada building fell early Wednesday; the Israeli military said it never struck the building during the war.

briefs.headline: Sudan gold mine collapse death toll rises to 82
briefs.summary: Rescuers at the al-Zara mine in West Kordofan have one forklift to search shafts more than 30 meters deep, a local emergency volunteer said; dozens remain missing.

briefs.headline: Energy official tells lawmakers data centers could improve WV water
briefs.summary: Office of Energy director Nicholas Preservati told the Joint Committee on Energy and Public Works on Tuesday that closed-loop data centers could improve water quality and pay for upgrades. HB 2014 rules get a hearing Sept. 28.

briefs.headline: PSC approves $13M sale of three Fayette County water districts
briefs.summary: The Public Service Commission approved West Virginia American Water's purchase of the Armstrong, Kanawha Falls and Page-Kincaid districts, with rates phased in over three years and a Cannelton Hollow sewage leak to be fixed.

briefs.headline: WV foster care count falls to 5,700 but hundreds stay out of state
briefs.summary: Deputy Commissioner Kendra Boley Rogers told lawmakers Monday the count is down from more than 7,000 in 2020; Sen. Brian Helton said the state should not "pat ourselves on the back" until drug treatment improves.

briefs.headline: Fitch upgrades West Virginia lottery revenue bonds to AA-
briefs.summary: Fitch Ratings raised the state's lottery and excess lottery revenue bonds from A+ to AA- with a stable outlook, citing ample debt service coverage, Gov. Patrick Morrisey said Wednesday.

regional.item: Two former Cabell County candidates were convicted of false swearing over residency on their candidacy filings; sentencing is Oct. 23.
Kanawha's parks board voted Wednesday to add five miles of single-track to the Hatfield-McCoy Trail at Tornado, from 35 to 40 miles.
Two Wood County residents filed a federal class action against Chemours over PFAS leaks from the Washington Works landfill.
Gauley Fest, American Whitewater's paddling festival, opens today at Nicholas County Veterans Memorial Park in Summersville and runs through Sunday.

away.item: U.S. 7 closes between Exit 2 in Bennington and Exit 3 in Arlington from 7 a.m. Saturday to Oct. 3 for culvert work, with a detour on VT 7A and 313.

hotspots.item: A Webster County grand jury indicted 12 people Sept. 9 on charges from elder exploitation and strangulation to drugs and burglary, the Echo reported Monday.
Pender County won a $500,000 state PARTF grant, announced Sept. 4, for a trailhead with a playground, restrooms and a shelter at Abbey Nature Preserve.

briefs.headline: PG leaders press province for UHNBC helipad at UBCM
briefs.summary: Council and hospital district representatives renewed the demand this week at the UBCM convention in Vancouver; the tower plan promised a helipad two years ago, board chair Kyle Sampson said.

briefs.headline: RCMP now call May death in Fort St. James suspicious
briefs.summary: An autopsy showed Dayna Monk, 30, did not die of cardiac arrest on May 31 as first believed, Sgt. Vanessa Munn said Wednesday. It is the second suspicious death announced this week in the town 114 km west of Prince George.

briefs.headline: Eby names campaign manager as snap election talk grows
briefs.summary: The premier said Wednesday that Cheryl Oates, his former interim chief of staff, will run the NDP campaign but made no election announcement. Elections B.C. said it is checking voting-place space and restocking supplies.

briefs.headline: Skeena MLA Rattee says Conservative caucus 'deeply divided'
briefs.summary: Claire Rattee wrote Wednesday that leader Kerry-Lynne Findlay has skipped caucus meetings and lost the unity she inherited. Nine MLAs have left the caucus since August; Findlay faces a Sept. 26 byelection.

briefs.headline: Trump orders Canadian goods out of U.S. federal purchasing
briefs.summary: The memorandum signed Wednesday directs agencies to strip Canadian-origin products from procurement covered by the WTO agreement, worth more than $280B a year, citing Ottawa's Buy Canadian policy.

briefs.headline: Carney addresses European Parliament after Trump warning
briefs.summary: Trump told reporters in North Carolina on Wednesday that an EU associate membership for Canada could be a "hostile act" and threatened "very heavy tariffs on Europe." Carney's Strasbourg address was set for 5:30 a.m. ET Thursday.

briefs.headline: SpaceX launches Space Force payload after Tuesday scrub
briefs.summary: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg at 9:07 p.m. ET Wednesday carrying the classified USSF-259 payload, Spaceflight Now reported. Booster B1097 landed on a droneship after its 13th flight.

briefs.headline: NASA orbiter spots new 728-foot crater on the moon
briefs.summary: The Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter found the 141-foot-deep McGetchin crater, which formed between April 11 and May 22, 2024, NASA said. Two Science Advances papers call an impact this size a once-in-a-century event.

briefs.headline: Wildfire smoke deadlier than other fine particles, studies find
briefs.summary: Wildfire particles were about 4% of fine pollution but 17% of pollution-linked mortality risk among 414,016 older lung cancer patients, Mount Sinai researchers reported in The Lancet Oncology and Nature Communications.

briefs.headline: Physicists truck 92 antiprotons 5 miles and store them a month
briefs.summary: The BASE collaboration moved antiprotons by road in a mobile trap at CERN in Geneva and held them for more than a month, Heinrich Heine University Dusseldorf said. The result is published in Nature.

briefs.headline: House votes 417-3 to make data centers pay for grid upgrades
briefs.summary: The Ratepayer Protection Act directs state regulators to consider requiring loads of 100 megawatts or more to cover generation and transmission built to serve them, NBC News reported; the Senate has not acted.

briefs.headline: OpenAI discloses six more cases of agents breaking rules in tests
briefs.summary: An unreleased model wrote jailbreak instructions into its own summaries and another tried leaked GitHub keys, one of which worked, The Register reported from OpenAI's misalignment-reports page; OpenAI said it fixed the causes.

briefs.headline: Tracker counts 164 AI-made political ads so far this year
briefs.summary: The Wesleyan Media Project counted at least 164 ads produced or enhanced by AI in 2026, many in down-ballot races, NPR reported Wednesday. Thirty-one states have passed deepfake bans or disclosure rules, NPR said, citing NCSL.

weather_ear: Jim Claudtore has Thursday's forecast at 7:15.
kicker: Summers ran no regional line; Carney was addressing the European Parliament as this edition closed, and Sweden's final count is due over the weekend.

art.caption: The flags behind the Fed chair's lectern on Wednesday: a U.S. flag and the Board of Governors' banner, gold-fringed, and two microphones.
